column3: A steaming bowl of ramen seen from above on the 64x64 panel: rich broth with glints of oil, a soft egg, nori sheets, scallions, chashu, a naruto fishcake swirl. The time is in the bowl: the noodles are lifted by chopsticks into the shapes of the numerals, or the hour is brushed on the nori and the minutes are noodles. Always alive: steam curls up (soft, translucent), oil droplets drift and merge on the broth, the broth ripples. Minute turn: chopsticks dip in and lift the old digit's noodles away in a long slurp, and new noodles are lowered and settle into the new numeral. Hour: a ladle of fresh broth swirls everything into a whirlpool and the toppings resettle.

A pinata party on a 64x128 tower: a colourful pinata hangs from a rope at the top, swinging and spinning with pendulum physics; the pinata IS the hour numeral (a papier-mache numeral wrapped in fringed crepe-paper stripes: design a festive fringed numeral set). Below, kids (bold silhouettes with sticks and party hats) and a pile of wrapped candies that the kids keep arranging into the minute numerals. Always alive: the pinata sways, the fringe flutters, kids hop and wave. Minute turn: a kid swings, whack, the pinata swings wildly, candy bursts out, and the kids scramble and rearrange the candy into the new minute. Hour: the pinata bursts open and a new hour pinata is lowered on its rope.

Dia de Muertos papel picado across the 256x64 banner: a string of cut tissue-paper flags in hot pink, orange, turquoise, yellow and purple, lit from behind so the cut-outs glow, each flag fluttering with a soft cloth ripple. The time is cut out of the flags: the numerals are the negative space of intricate cut paper (flowers, calaveras, scroll borders round them); design cut-paper numerals with lacy bridges that still read boldly. Always alive: the string sags and swings, flags billow in waves of wind, marigold petals drift down, candles flicker below. Minute turn: the old digit's flag is unpinned and blows away twirling, and a new flag slides along the string into place. Hour: a gust makes the whole string snap and dance.

The three panels on a diagonal are an escalator in a department store, rising from bottom-left to top-right. The steps move constantly (real escalator steps forming at the bottom and flattening at the top, the rubber handrail sliding). Riders carry the time: four big numerals ride up on the steps (giant boxed numerals on a delivery trolley, numeral balloons, or the numerals themselves as characters with legs), and each one holds its place by walking down exactly as fast as the escalator rises: the joke is that the time is running to stand still. Minute turn: the old digit steps off at the top and strolls away, the new one steps on at the bottom and rides up into its slot. Hour: a sale crowd floods the escalator.

A Ferris wheel at a fairground at dusk filling the 192x192 frame around the missing centre panel: rim and gondolas run through the frame, spokes reach inward into the dark hole (the hub hidden in the night). Gondolas carry the time: lit gondolas with big marquee-bulb numerals (design bulb numerals), the wheel turning slowly so they glide along the frame, and timed so the right gondolas reach the reading positions (draw them: a loading platform for the minutes, a top for the hour). Always alive: the wheel turns, gondolas swing as they go, chasing lights on the spokes, a crowd queues. Hour: fireworks burst behind the wheel.

A busy city crossroads seen from above: the plus shape is the intersection, four roads meeting in the centre panel with zebra crossings and traffic lights. Cars, buses, taxis, bikes and pedestrians flow in turns with the lights (bold top-down vehicles with roofs and windscreens, headlights and taillights at night). The time is road paint: each arm holds one huge numeral painted on the asphalt (design road-marking numerals: thermoplastic white with worn edges and tyre marks across them). Minute turn: a road crew truck drives in, the old numeral is ground off in a dust cloud, and a line-painting machine sprays the new one stroke by stroke while cars wait. Hour: rush-hour gridlock, horns, the lights all flash.

A card stunt in a stadium: the 192x192 square is a stand packed with people, each holding up a coloured card, and together the cards make a giant picture: the time. Up close it is a crowd (each card is a small tile with a hand and a head peeking over it), from across the room it is a giant crisp mosaic of the time with a pattern behind. Always alive: a Mexican wave rolls through the crowd (cards tilt and flash), people fidget, someone drops a card and grabs it again. Minute turn: the cards flip in a sweeping wave to form the new number, each card turning in perspective. Hour: a full show: the crowd plays a fireworks animation, then the time returns.

A vending machine, 128x192 portrait: glass front, spiral coils in rows, snacks and cans, price labels, a keypad and coin slot at the side, the delivery bin at the bottom, lit inside with a cold fluorescent glow. The time is on the snacks: the front products carry the numerals as their packaging (design packaging numerals in snack-brand typography, a different snack per digit: crisps, a candy bar, a soda can...). Always alive: the tube light flickers, a coil wiggles, reflections slide over the glass, a moth bumps the light. Minute turn: an unseen customer keys in a code (the keypad lights), the coil of the old digit turns and the snack tilts and drops into the bin with a thud, and the next snack slides forward showing the new numeral; now and then one gets stuck and the machine is shaken. Hour: restock: the door swings open and the rows are refilled.

A salmon run up a waterfall, 64x192 tower: the falls pour over rocky ledges in white water and spray, a brown bear stands on the top ledge, paws ready, and salmon leap up the falls in shining arcs. The time lives on the falls: the hours in a high pool, the minutes in a low one, formed by resting salmon schools or by the rock ledges with the water pouring round them. Always alive: the water flows, mist drifts, fish leap constantly, the bear fidgets. Minute turn: a big salmon makes a heroic leap up to its slot as the new digit forms, while the bear swipes the old one out of the water. Hour: the bear catches a giant salmon and roars.

A dollhouse cutaway in the L-shaped assembly (128x128 with the top-right panel missing): two floors on the left, a ground-floor wing on the right; tiny rooms with wallpaper, furniture, lamps, a staircase, and a family of little dolls living in it. Push for the time to be made from the house itself: e.g. a toddler doll scribbles the numerals in crayon across the walls and a parent doll scrubs the old one off each minute, or the furniture is arranged into digits, or the lit rooms at night. Always alive: dolls walk room to room, lights switch on and off, a kettle steams, a cat stretches on the stairs. Minute turn: the crayon toddler is caught, the old digit scrubbed away, and the new one scribbled while the parent's back is turned. Hour: a party, everyone gathers in one room with a cake.
